scope: Public metadata and official repository/catalog evidence only; no C13+ ground truth or model outcomes accessed.

observations: 104 atomic metadata entries are technique-level and are not independent attack chains.
Nine compound metadata entries were identified: GoldenSAML, seven LSASS campaigns, and Log4Shell.
The existing OTRF APT29 Day 1 development campaign remains separately excluded by the used-campaign registry.
Technique and malware metadata entries are not automatically campaign executions.
One apt_simulations scenario was identified: ActiveMQ exploitation followed by LockBit.
The release documents eight testbeds with multi-stage attack sequences, host logs, PCAP, and separate ground truth.
The eight testbeds are fox, harrison, russellmitchell, santos, shaw, wardbeck, wheeler, and wilson.
AIT Alert Data Set and Kyoushi derivatives do not add independent campaign executions.
The release reports seven scenario families and 34 simulation archives.
The 34 archives are parameterized runs of seven scenario families and therefore count as at most seven chains.
The author dataset contains six PCAP files but explicitly defines only two multi-step attack scenarios.
The files and attack stages are components of those two scenarios, not six independent chains.
The abstract states that ATLASv2 replicates ten attack scenarios.
A publisher-controlled raw data artifact was not verified during this audit; third-party mirrors are insufficient for hash-bound intake.
The paper describes one seven-day IIoT collection spanning multiple APT phases and more than 20 techniques.
Attack techniques and phases within that collection are not separate independent campaigns.
The author metadata describes network traffic collected over five days as an accelerated APT timeline.
The five days are stages of one campaign, not five independent campaign cases.
The paper reports 70 attack sessions designed from 50 different scenarios.
A session is a 20-minute capture; repeated sessions do not increase the unique scenario-family count beyond 50.
No verifiable public data artifact was linked from the article page during this audit, so its current hash-bound intake contribution is zero.
DARPA E3 and E5 each describe one engagement observed by multiple TA1 performers.
Performer streams, hosts, and time slices are repeated views of an engagement, not independent campaigns.
E3, E5, and OpTC were already used in Project05 development cases and are excluded from C13+ intake.
